issues.legal_issue: The customary rule governing succession to the religious institution’s property and office was proved, including the devolution of a line’s interest to the surviving lines when its last representative had no eligible immediate successor.
material_facts: The evidence showed repeated succession from a Mahant to his Chela, and, when that successor was unavailable, to the Mahant’s Gurbhai or the Gurbhai’s Chela.
When the last representative of another line died without a Chela or an eligible Gurbhai or Chela of a Gurbhai, representatives of the two surviving lines inherited that line’s interest.
Other Chelas of earlier Mahants in the extinct line were alive, but did not claim succession; a Chela of an earlier Mahant who was more remotely related to the last representative also made no claim.
The evidence indicated that Mahants could initiate several Chelas, and there had been no election to the office of Mahant.
issues.conclusion: The asserted custom was established: a Mahant was succeeded by his Chela, or, if there was no eligible Chela, by his Gurbhai or the Gurbhai’s Chela; if the last representative of a line died without any such successor, that line’s interest passed to the representatives of the surviving lines. The appeal was allowed and the trial court’s decree in the claimant’s favour was restored.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed customary succession from the position at the death of the last representative of the particular line: only that representative’s Chela or other eligible immediate successor could inherit within the line, and the existence of Chelas of earlier Mahants did not prevent the line from becoming extinct. Because extinction of a line would be rare, a single instance of succession on extinction could suffice to establish that part of the custom. The Court relied on the evidence of actual successions and the circumstances surrounding the earlier extinction and cited no statutory provision or earlier case.

rule.if: customary_succession_appeal and ordinary_succession_patterns and prior_extinction_transfer and last_holder_lacked_eligible_successor and surviving_line_representatives

predicates.customary_succession_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal in a dispute over succession asserted to be governed by a customary rule.
predicates.ordinary_succession_patterns: Actual successions within the institution repeatedly followed the pattern of a Mahant’s Chela succeeding, with an eligible co-disciple or that co-disciple’s Chela succeeding when appropriate.
predicates.prior_extinction_transfer: A prior line’s last representative died without an eligible immediate successor, and representatives of the surviving lines inherited that line’s interest.
predicates.last_holder_lacked_eligible_successor: The last representative in the disputed line died without a Chela, an eligible co-disciple, or a Chela of an eligible co-disciple to succeed.
predicates.surviving_line_representatives: Representatives of other lines remained available to inherit the interest of the line that had no eligible successor.

issues.definition: When the proceeding is a customary succession appeal and the ordinary succession patterns, prior extinction transfer, absence of an eligible successor, and surviving line representatives are established, the customary lineage succession rule is proved.
